context.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform managing patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals. It ensures high availability (99.99%), HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and sub-second EMR performance.

## Key Elements
* Patients, Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, and Hospital Administrators
* External Systems: Insurance Clearinghouses and External Labs/Imaging Vendors
* Containers: API Gateway, EMR Service, Scheduling Service, Billing Service, and Asynchronous Queues
* Infrastructure: On-premises Kubernetes cluster and AWS (`eu-central-1`)

## Relationships
* Users interact via web/mobile frontends using HTTPS and TLS 1.3
* Internal microservices communicate via mTLS-secured gRPC and REST APIs
* External Labs/Imaging integrate via HL7 FHIR APIs over TLS 1.3
* Insurance Clearinghouses integrate via secure REST APIs with OAuth 2.1 authentication
* Hybrid synchronization uses encrypted IPSec tunnels and low-latency interconnects

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: Container orchestration deployed across on-prem and AWS for active-active high availability (R-06)
* AES-256: Data encryption at rest for databases and queued payloads to satisfy HIPAA/GDPR (R-05)
* AWS KMS & On-Premises HSM: Segregated cryptographic key management to enforce data residency rules
* TLS 1.3 & mTLS: Network security protocol ensuring zero unauthenticated node communication
* HL7 FHIR: Interoperability standard for lab and imaging system integration (R-08)
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing stack for monitoring EMR performance and load times under 1 second (R-07)

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture pairs on-premises data control with cloud scalability to meet strict regulatory and uptime mandates. Robust resilience patterns—including circuit breakers and segregated key management—guarantee continuous clinical operations and data security.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed for medium-sized hospitals and clinics to securely handle patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing. It ensures strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance, 99.99% availability, and long-term data retention.

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Patients, Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, Hospital Administrators
* **External Systems:** Insurance Clearinghouses, External Labs/Imaging Vendors
* **Containers:** API Gateway, Patient Portal Container, EMR Container, Scheduling Container, Billing Container, Notification Container, Analytics & Reporting Container, WAF Container
* **Infrastructure/Data:** On-Premises Kubernetes Cluster, AWS (eu-central-1), PostgreSQL Databases (Patroni/etcd), Kafka/RabbitMQ Event Broker, Immutable Audit Storage Sink, HashiCorp Vault

## Relationships
* **Patients/Users to API Gateway / WAF:** HTTPS (TLS 1.3), OAuth2/OIDC, Multi-Factor Authentication
* **Containers to Containers:** mTLS via SPIFFE/SPIRE, gRPC / REST APIs
* **Core Containers to Event Broker:** Asynchronous message publishing/consuming via Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ
* **Containers to External Systems:** Secure HTTPS REST APIs and HL7 FHIR protocols for lab, imaging, and insurance clearinghouses
* **Databases to Storage:** Active-Passive replication with field-level encryption for PHI

## Technology Stack
* **Orchestration:** Kubernetes (hybrid on-prem and AWS eu-central-1) for container management
* **Deployment:** ArgoCD (GitOps) for repeatable, audit-compliant deployments
* **Security & Auth:** OAuth2/OIDC, SPIFFE/SPIRE for mTLS, HashiCorp Vault for hardware-backed AES-256 key management
* **Messaging:** Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ for asynchronous, decoupled event-driven integration
* **Database:** PostgreSQL with Patroni/etcd for high-availability active-passive clustering
* **Interoperability:** HL7 FHIR APIs for standardized healthcare data exchange

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture balances strict HIPAA/GDPR data residency mandates with high availability (99.99%) through an active-passive regional database topology. Field-level PHI encryption and strict container segmentation protect sensitive health data without sacrificing the sub-second EMR performance required by clinicians.

## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed for medium-sized hospitals and clinics to securely handle patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing. It enforces strict HIPAA and GDPR compliance while maintaining 99.99% high availability and high-performance clinical workflows.

## Key Elements
- Patients, Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, and Hospital Administrators (Primary Users)
- WAF Container (Web Application Firewall at perimeter)
- API Gateway (Kubernetes Ingress / Gateway API)
- Patient Portal, EMR, Scheduling, Billing, Notification, and Analytics & Reporting Containers
- PostgreSQL Databases (with Patroni/etcd), Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ Event Broker, HashiCorp Vault (AES-256)
- External Systems: Insurance Clearinghouses, External Labs/Imaging Vendors

## Relationships
- Users -> WAF Container: Accesses system securely via HTTPS [HTTPS (TLS 1.3), OAuth2/OIDC, MFA]
- WAF Container -> API Gateway: Forwards filtered traffic securely [mTLS]
- EMR Container -> HL7 FHIR APIs: Exchanges lab and imaging data with external systems [HL7 FHIR REST/JSON]
- Containers -> PostgreSQL Databases / HashiCorp Vault: Persists records and fetches encrypted secrets [TLS, AES-256]

## Technology Stack
- Kubernetes (on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1): Hybrid cloud orchestration ensuring active-active 99.99% uptime.
- PostgreSQL with Patroni/etcd: High-availability relational storage for strict data integrity and 10-year retention.
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Event broker for asynchronous messaging across microservices.
- HashiCorp Vault: Secrets management enforcing AES-256 encryption at rest.
- OWASP Core Rule Set & In-Memory Redaction: Perimeter security protecting against OWASP threats while masking PHI.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid Kubernetes deployment with an mTLS-secured WAF and API Gateway perimeter to guarantee 99.99% availability and strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance. Decoupled microservices backed by encrypted PostgreSQL and Kafka ensure high-performance EMR rendering under 1 second while safely managing sensitive healthcare workloads.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It provides secure, high-availability clinical IT operations while maintaining strict HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients, Receptionists, Clinicians, Billing Specialists, Hospital Administrators
- Insurance Clearinghouses, External Labs/Imaging Vendors
- API Gateway (Kubernetes Ingress / Gateway API)
- WAF Container
- Patient Portal Container
- EMR Container, Scheduling Container, Billing Container, Notification Container, Analytics & Reporting Container
- PostgreSQL Databases (Patroni/etcd), Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ Event Broker, Immutable Audit Storage Sink, HashiCorp Vault

## Relationships
- WAF Container -> API Gateway: Forwards filtered traffic via HTTPS
- API Gateway -> Patient Portal, EMR, Scheduling, Billing, and Analytics Containers: Routes client requests via HTTPS with mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE)
- API Gateway -> Redis Cache: Performs local authorization caching and token validation
- API Gateway -> HashiCorp Vault: Retrieves secrets and manages automated TLS lifecycles via cert-manager

## Technology Stack
- Kubernetes & Hybrid Cloud (on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1): Enables high availability (99.99%) and active-active multi-region deployment.
- API Gateway (Kubernetes Ingress / Gateway API): Enforces OWASP top 10 guardrails, OAuth2/OIDC validation, and persona-based rate limiting.
- HashiCorp Vault & cert-manager: Manages AES-256 encryption at rest, SVID generation, and automated TLS certificate rotation.
- Distributed Redis: Provides fast local authorization caching to maintain sub-second P95 latencies.
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Captures distributed traces and metrics across the zero-trust mesh.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid active-active deployment with an advanced API Gateway to meet strict 99.99% availability and sub-second P95 performance constraints. Centralizing security, OAuth2 validation, rate limiting, and mTLS at the gateway guarantees HIPAA and GDPR compliance while protecting core microservices from volumetric and application-layer threats.

HashiCorp Vault.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the HashiCorp Vault container"
parentContainer:
  name: "HashiCorp Vault"
elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Vault Core Engine"
    technology: "HashiCorp Vault Go Runtime"
    description: "Core security engine responsible for processing cryptographic operations and authorization."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Transit Secrets Engine"
    technology: "Vault Cryptographic Module"
    description: "Provides cryptographic functions as a service, including AES-256 encryption for sensitive data."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Database Secrets Engine"
    technology: "Vault Dynamic Credential Provider"
    description: "Generates dynamic database credentials on-demand for backend services like EMR and Billing."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Vault Agent Sidecars"
    technology: "Vault Agent (Daemon)"
    description: "Runs alongside backend containers to handle secure secret retrieval and token renewal."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Audit Device"
    technology: "Vault Syslog Streamer"
    description: "Streams comprehensive audit logs to the immutable audit storage sink."
relationships:
  - source: "Vault Agent Sidecars"
    destination: "Vault Core Engine"
    description: "Retrieves secrets and keys via gRPC/mTLS"
  - source: "Vault Core Engine"
    destination: "Transit Secrets Engine"
    description: "Executes encryption/decryption requests"
  - source: "Vault Core Engine"
    destination: "Database Secrets Engine"
    description: "Manages dynamic credentials"
  - source: "Vault Core Engine"
    destination: "Audit Device"
    description: "Logs security events"
  - source: "Audit Device"
    destination: "Immutable Audit Storage Sink"
    description: "Streams audit logs via Syslog/TCP"
HashiCorp Vault.diagram:
@startuml
!include https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plantuml-stdlib/C4-PlantUML/master/C4_Component.puml
LAYOUT_WITH_LEGEND()

title Component diagram for the HashiCorp Vault container

System_Ext(Immutable Audit Storage Sink, "Immutable Audit Storage Sink", "External storage system for audit logs.")

Container_Boundary(vault_container, "HashiCorp Vault") {
    Component(Vault Core Engine, "Vault Core Engine", "HashiCorp Vault Go Runtime", "Core security engine responsible for processing cryptographic operations and authorization.")
    Component(Transit Secrets Engine, "Transit Secrets Engine", "Vault Cryptographic Module", "Provides cryptographic functions as a service, including AES-256 encryption for sensitive data.")
    Component(Database Secrets Engine, "Database Secrets Engine", "Vault Dynamic Credential Provider", "Generates dynamic database credentials on-demand for backend services like EMR and Billing.")
    Component(Vault Agent Sidecars, "Vault Agent Sidecars", "Vault Agent (Daemon)", "Runs alongside backend containers to handle secure secret retrieval and token renewal.")
    Component(Audit Device, "Audit Device", "Vault Syslog Streamer", "Streams comprehensive audit logs to the immutable audit storage sink.")
}

Rel(Vault Agent Sidecars, Vault Core Engine, "Retrieves secrets and keys", "gRPC/mTLS")
Rel(Vault Core Engine, Transit Secrets Engine, "Executes encryption/decryption requests")
Rel(Vault Core Engine, Database Secrets Engine, "Manages dynamic credentials")
Rel(Vault Core Engine, Audit Device, "Logs security events")
Rel(Audit Device, Immutable Audit Storage Sink, "Streams audit logs", "Syslog/TCP")

@enduml
